_comment: Maternity page FAQ. The timing answer must never read as medical advice.
title: Questions about maternity sessions

questions.a: Somewhere around 28 to 34 weeks is a common sweet spot, but there's no single right time. Earlier usually means easier movement and a smaller bump. Later gives you the fuller, more traditional maternity shape. Your comfort and how your pregnancy is actually going matter more than a number — this is a general guide, not a rule.

questions.q: Who can be in the photographs?
questions.a: Whoever you want. Just you, you and your partner, your older children, your dog. Plenty of people do a mix — some of just her, then some with everyone.

questions.q: What should I wear? Do I have to do a bare belly?
questions.a: Only if you want to. A flowing dress, ordinary clothes you feel good in, bare belly, covered belly — all of it works, and none of it is expected. Solids tend to photograph particularly well because they keep the attention where you want it. You'll supply your own clothing.

questions.q: Can we do this at home instead of outdoors?
questions.a: Sometimes, yes — a nursery can be lovely if the light and the space work. Otherwise we use the same locations as any other session. Ask me and we'll figure out what suits.

questions.q: Can I bring things that mean something?
questions.a: Yes, and I'd encourage it. Baby shoes, an ultrasound image, a rattle, a personalized blanket if you know the name and you're announcing it. I have an announcement message board you're welcome to use.

We usually do the maternity photographs first, then bring them in. That way the images of you are done before anyone runs out of patience, and the ones with them still feel relaxed rather than rushed.

questions.q: I'm not sure what style I want.
questions.a: That's normal. I keep Pinterest boards for exactly this — scroll through and notice what pulls you in and what makes you cringe. Both are useful. Send me a handful of either and we'll plan from there.
